items.q: Spec for a pumped M25 slab pour: slump 100 mm +/- 25 mm. The transit mixer arrives and the slump cone test reads 150 mm. What do you do?
options: Wait 30 minutes for it to stiffen, then pour
Hold the truck and reject the batch; it is outside 75-125 mm
Accept it; a wetter mix pumps more easily
Add a bag of cement into the drum and accept
items.explain: Slump outside the specified range means the water-cement ratio is not what was designed, so the batch is rejected rather than adjusted on site.

items.q: A 150 mm concrete cube fails in the compression testing machine at 630 kN. What compressive strength do you record?
items.explain: Strength = load / area = 630,000 N / (150 x 150 mm2) = 28 N/mm2, which passes for M25 concrete.

items.q: A roof slab was cast with PPC (blended cement) in May at a hot, dry site. The contractor wants to stop water curing after 7 days. Per IS 456, is that acceptable?
options: No, at least 10 days for blended cement or hot dry weather
No, curing must continue for 28 days
Yes, if the slab looks dry and hard
Yes, 7 days is the code minimum in all cases
items.explain: IS 456 asks for a minimum of 7 days for OPC in normal conditions but at least 10 days where mineral admixtures or blended cements are used or in hot dry weather.

items.q: A 12 mm bar in a BBS is bent 300 + 3000 + 300 mm with two 90 degree bends. What cutting length do you enter?
items.explain: Deduct 2d for each 90 degree bend: 3600 - 2 x (2 x 12) = 3552 mm; forgetting the deduction over-orders steel on every bar.

items.q: Steel arrives in 12 m lengths. Approximately how much does one 16 mm dia bar weigh?
items.explain: Unit weight = d^2 / 162 kg/m = 256 / 162 = 1.58 kg/m, so a 12 m bar is about 19 kg; this is how site steel reconciliation is done.

items.q: The site folder has a tender drawing (R0) and a GFC drawing (R2) for the same slab, with different bar spacing. Which one do you build from?
options: Whichever gives closer spacing, to be safe
GFC R2, the latest issued-for-construction revision
Tender R0, since the contract was signed on it
Neither, wait for the consultant to visit
items.explain: Only Good For Construction drawings at their latest revision are built from; tender drawings are for pricing and are superseded.

items.q: A worker must enter an underground sump to clean out sludge. What must be in place before entry?
options: Helmet, shoes and a toolbox talk are enough
A rope tied to the worker's waist
Confined-space permit, gas test, and a standby attendant outside
items.explain: A sump is a confined space: the permit-to-work, gas testing for oxygen and toxic gases, and a standby person are mandatory, not optional PPE extras.

items.q: A slab is 12 m x 8 m x 150 mm thick. What quantity of concrete do you record in the measurement book?
items.explain: 12 x 8 x 0.15 = 14.4 m3; convert the thickness to metres before multiplying, and 96 is only the area in m2.

items.q: A 230 mm thick brick wall is 10 m long and 3 m high, with one door opening 1 m x 2.1 m. What brickwork quantity is billed?
items.explain: Net area = 30 - 2.1 = 27.9 m2, times 0.23 m thickness = 6.42 m3; openings are deducted and the answer is in m3, not m2.

items.q: Which entry belongs in the site daily log and is actually useful when a delay claim comes up later?
options: Labour count, weather, materials received, work done and instructions received, with times
items.explain: The daily log is the site's evidence record, so it captures what happened, when, with what resources and under whose instruction.

items.q: Per IS 456 sampling frequency, how many cube samples must be taken for a single 24 m3 pour?
items.explain: IS 456 requires 1 sample for 1-5 m3, 2 for 6-15 m3, 3 for 16-30 m3 and 4 for 31-50 m3, each sample being three cubes.
